tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the user's own past Claude Code sessions, by words and by meaning, on this machine. Use it before debugging an error or redoing work that may already have been done, and when the user asks what was decided or tried before. An exact error string, function name or path is the strongest query. The earlier turns of this session are searched too, up to the turn in progress, and come back marked `this session, earlier`. Words about time in the query are read, not matched: `yesterday`, `last week`, `since friday`, `sept 21` set the span, `latest` asks for the newest matches, and a query about time alone (`what did we do yesterday`) lists the sessions of that time. Returns the best matching sessions, newest first, each with the start of its id, the files it changed, and every match inside its turn: `asked` is the prompt that opened the turn, `ended` the last thing Claude said in it, and `reply` what the user typed next, which tells whether the answer held. Pass the id as `session` to read the session in order; `kind` narrows that to, say, user and assistant. Mode `fix` takes an error text and returns what past sessions ran right after the same error. Mode `how` takes words of a shell command and returns the commands that were run, the most run first. Mode `blame` takes a file path, or the end of one, and returns the sessions that changed that file with what the user had asked for. A last line that names an offset means there is more: call again with that `offset`.
